newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate down on demand for paper.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate down on demand for paper.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were down 50 basis points at 21.50 percent in early trade on Tuesday. Traders and analysts said low inflation data released the day before triggered demand for paper.
"Rates are declining further and in theory should edge down a little more," a fixed-income analyst said.
Foreign exchange dealers noted that brokers were selling dollars to invest in the money market, for which reason benchmark 48-hour contracts had firmed 1.45 centavos to 7.9650/7.9680 per dollar.

Banco de Mexico announced shortly after the close of money market trading on Monday that consumer prices had risen by 0.91 percent in May, the first time monthly inflation had been less than one percent since the December 1994 peso devaluation crisis.
Overnight rates on bank paper were meanwhile down 40 basis points at 22.60 percent.
Liquidity of 178 million pesos was due to flow back to the market during the session from prior central bank participation.
